newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's electronics rise sharply in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's electronics rise sharply in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan's electronic shares, fuelled by Nasdaq's recent rally and strong fundementals, rebounded sharply in late trade on Thursday from tumbles on Tuesday and Wednesday, brokers said.
With 50 minutes left, the heavily weighted electronics had risen 4.47 percent.
United Microelectronics soared by the daily seven-percent limit or T$7.50 to T$120, and most other electronics shares also saw handsome gains.
"Considering the sector had fallen for five consecutive sessions, it is time for a rebound given the strong fundementals of the industry," said Ben Lee, analyst for Nomura Securities.
Brokers said recent rallies by U.S. tech index Nasdaq also helped boost sentiment.
Another chip giant, Taiwan Semiconductors, was up T$6.5 to T$140.5 -- recovering from its T$5 loss on Wednesday.
Computer maker Acer rose T$4 to T$94, while chipmaker Winbond was up T$2 to T$64.
